title: Superscript and subscript
learningObjectives: Choose semantic text elements and inspect their browser output

understand.concept: sup places text above the baseline and sub places it below, for conventional notation such as exponents and chemical formulas. Do not use them merely to shrink text.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct notation preserves meaning in mathematics and science content.
understand.analogy: A book uses headings, paragraphs and notes for different purposes; HTML gives those roles explicit structure.
understand.analogyLimit: The book analogy is a memory aid; a browser parses HTML according to defined rules.

explain.narrative: sup places text above the baseline and sub places it below, for conventional notation such as exponents and chemical formulas. Do not use them merely to shrink text.

examples.explanation: Each element gives meaning to its content. Render it in a browser and observe how changing an element affects meaning and presentation.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser displays the corresponding heading, paragraph, inline formatting or text structure.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect the H3.6 concept in the starter code and add one more example.
practise.independentTask: Write a short semantic article on a topic you choose; use CSS rather than misusing HTML for visual spacing.
hints: Choose elements for their meaning, not their default appearance.
